subject: dbw
fixes: c-dbw-normal-forms math (highest-normal-form procedure, step 5): the 2NF test looked only at the FDs of F ('no violating FD with a non-prime right side has a left side that is a proper subset of a key'), which wrongly certifies 2NF when a partial dependency is implied but not listed. Counterexample: R(A,B,C,D), F = {A->C, C->A, AC->D} has keys AB and BC; no FD of F has its left side inside a key, yet A->D is implied and is partial. A python3 brute force over 60,000 random FD sets found that checking only F agrees with F+ for BCNF and 3NF in every case but disagrees for 2NF in 201 cases. Step 5 now computes the closure of every proper subset of each candidate key and cites the counterexample.

f-dbw-normal-form-conditions meaning: 'To test the given relation for BCNF it is enough to check the FDs of F' now says 'BCNF or 3NF' (verified by the same brute force) and adds that the shortcut fails for 2NF, with the same counterexample and the correct test (closures of the proper subsets of each candidate key). whenToUse changed from 'test the FDs against BCNF, then 3NF, then 2NF' to 'test the FDs of F against BCNF, then 3NF; for 2NF, check the closures of the proper subsets of each candidate key'.

c-dbw-sql-aggregation-nulls math: 'On an empty set, or on values that are all NULL, COUNT gives 0' was wrong for COUNT(*) when the rows exist but every value is NULL (COUNT(*) counts those rows). It now separates the cases: with no GROUP BY, an empty input gives COUNT(*) = COUNT(A) = 0 and NULL for SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX; all-NULL values give COUNT(A) = 0 and NULL aggregates, while COUNT(*) still counts the rows. Checked in sqlite3 on the concept's own Emp table (dept C: COUNT(bonus) = 0, COUNT(*) = 1).

f-dbw-data-normalization meaning and c-dbw-data-transformation intuition: 'increasing linear maps' -> 'increasing affine maps v' = av + b with a > 0'. Min-max and z-score have an offset, so they are affine, not linear. The formula card also states the condition new_max > new_min needed for min-max to be increasing, and the concept's 'they change only the units' -> 'they change only the scale and the origin'.

f-dbw-cube-cuboids-cells meaning (Schemas): 'each fact-table row is one non-empty base cell, so the fact table has at most prod|D_i| rows' made conditional on the fact table being stored at base-cuboid grain (at most one row per combination of dimension keys); added that a transaction-level fact table can repeat a combination.
f-dbw-sampling meaning: stratified sampling 'the usual choice for skewed data' -> 'especially useful for skewed data' (textbook wording; 'usual choice' was unsupported).
